cards.title: Advertorial Fundamentals and the Don't-Rewrite-a-Swipe Rule
cards.summary: What an advertorial is and why asking AI to rewrite a competitor's ad without foundational research produces low-converting copy.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to produce a long-form advertorial landing page for paid traffic rather than a standard product page.
steps: Understand the format: an advertorial blends an ad with an editorial so the page reads like it was written by a third-party, impartial source, while actually selling the product down the page.
Define the funnel role: the advertorial is typically the landing page that paid traffic hits before the sales page or offer, so it must carry the story and belief-shifting, not just product features.

Reject the common shortcut of finding a successful competitor advertorial and prompting an LLM to 'rewrite this but for my company' — the source calls this a terrible strategy because it skips research on your product, audience and offer.

Accept the sequencing: research first, foundational documents second, swipe third, draft fourth, edit ('chief') fifth. The source states this full process took roughly under an hour to complete an advertorial for the demoed product.
Apply to your store by treating every advertorial as built on your own customer research, not as a text-substitution exercise on someone else's asset.
caveats: The five-step framework, prompts and swipe material are the presenter's opinionated SOP; adapt them rather than treating step order as mandatory.
The 'under an hour' figure is the presenter's own example, not a benchmark for your store.

cards.title: The Five-Step AI Advertorial SOP
cards.summary: Overview of the five-stage AI workflow for producing advertorials: research, foundational docs, swipe, draft, chief.
cards.use_when: Planning production capacity for paid-traffic advertorial landing pages and deciding where in the workflow to invest human time.
steps: Step 1 — Research: use AI (ChatGPT with Deep Research) to gather qualitative customer research rather than doing it manually.
Step 2 — Foundational docs: turn the research into a reusable document set (research doc, avatar sheet, offer brief, necessary beliefs) that you feed into the model on every future copy task.
Step 3 — Swipe: find a currently successful competitor advertorial and upload it as a structural reference for the rewrite.
Step 4 — Draft: have AI write the advertorial in sequence (first half, then second half) using the foundational docs plus the swipe.
Step 5 — Chief (edit): have AI evaluate the draft against the foundational docs, then personally read and fix friction points before spending money on traffic.
Note the source's claim that the foundational documents are reusable: once built, they can drive advertorials, VSLs, ads and other landing page copy for the same brand.
caveats: The presenter asserts the foundational-docs step is the one most people skip and the reason their AI copy fails; this is his diagnosis, not a measured finding.
Document formats and model features change — verify the current ChatGPT interface and model version before relying on any specific feature.

cards.title: Grounding AI in Your Product Before Prompting
cards.summary: Upload your sales page and existing copy as PDFs so the model writes from real product context instead of generic assumptions.
cards.use_when: Preparing inputs before generating advertorial or landing page copy for a specific product.
steps: Convert your product's sales page to PDF (the source used a webpage-to-PDF tool) and upload it into the chat as product context.
Upload any other owned content you have: existing advertorials, ad copy, PDFs of current pages — the source advises giving 'as much information as possible on the product itself.'
Add a short plain-language line in the prompt explaining what you're selling and to whom, filling in the placeholder in the template prompt.
Upload the two copywriting-research reference documents the SOP links to, which the source says sharpen the model's qualitative research.
Treat input quality as the ceiling on output quality: the source's position is that complaints about AI writing bad copy usually reflect poor prompting and thin inputs, not the model itself.
caveats: The presenter prefers GPT-4.5 over GPT-4 and over Claude for this workflow; model quality claims are his personal experience and may be outdated.
Verify the current model names and file-upload behaviour in your tool — interfaces change.

cards.title: AI Inception: Making the Model Write Its Own Deep Research Prompt
cards.summary: Prompt ChatGPT to generate the Deep Research prompt itself so the customer research scrape is as comprehensive as possible.
cards.use_when: Running customer research for a new advertorial, new offer or new market entry before writing any landing page copy.
steps: After priming the chat with product context, paste a prompt instructing the model to write a research prompt for its own Deep Research feature — the source calls this 'AI inception.'
Copy the generated prompt verbatim and paste it back into the chat with Deep Research mode selected.
Answer the clarifying questions the model asks (in the demo: US-based audience, all price ranges, and a framing question) so it has scoping constraints.
Let the Deep Research run — the source notes it typically takes roughly 8–20 minutes depending on product and market; his example returned in about 11 minutes.
Save the resulting research output as a document and download it as a PDF; this becomes the first foundational document.
caveats: Deep Research availability, duration and behaviour are version-dependent; confirm the feature exists in your plan before building the workflow around it.
The 8–20 minute window is the presenter's observed range, not a standard.

cards.title: Building the Avatar Sheet from AI Research
cards.summary: Convert the raw research document into a structured avatar sheet with demographics, pain points and verbatim customer quotes.
cards.use_when: Creating the audience profile that will drive advertorial messaging, hooks and headline angles for a specific product.
steps: Take your saved research document plus an avatar-sheet template prompt and upload both into the chat.
Have the model fill the template from the research rather than inventing audience detail — the source stresses the sheet must be grounded in the scraped research.

Capture demographics and, critically, direct customer quotes pulled from the research; the demo surfaced lines like worry about another freezing winter and frustration at wasting money on inefficient heating.
Treat those quotes as raw material for the advertorial: the source notes the quotes expose the pain you'll tap in the copy.
Save the completed sheet as a document, download it as a PDF, and file it as foundational document number two.
Reuse the same sheet across future copy for that avatar; changing product but not audience means you can skip rebuilding it.
caveats: The sheet's usefulness depends entirely on the breadth of the upstream research; thin research yields a generic avatar.
The demo product and quotes are the presenter's example, not evidence about your market.
cards.source_name: how i write advertorial landing pages that make me $1.3m_mo only using AI (prompts included).docx

cards.title: The Offer Brief: Funnel Architecture, Awareness and Unique Mechanism
cards.summary: Build an offer document capturing funnel architecture, stage of awareness, sophistication and unique mechanism before drafting copy.
cards.use_when: Preparing to write an advertorial or sales page and needing to pin down what offer, at which stage of awareness, the copy must carry.
steps: Upload the offer-brief template prompt plus your existing offer materials into the chat and have the model complete it from the research and product context.
Record the funnel architecture you intend to use — what page the advertorial feeds and what offer sits behind it.
Specify the level of consciousness / stage of awareness and stage of sophistication you are speaking to, so tone and mechanism depth match the audience.
Define the unique mechanism — the specific reason your product works that the copy will carry — because the source treats this as a core copy ingredient in the advertorial and VSL.
Save and download as a PDF; this is foundational document number three.
Add extra detail beyond the template where you have it — the source reiterates output quality tracks input quality.
caveats: This is a copy-briefing device, not a substitute for real positioning work; the source's point is that blind swiping without understanding these principles is why copy fails.
Stage-of-awareness labels are commonly used heuristics; do not treat them as fixed numeric bands.

cards.title: The Necessary Beliefs Document (Max Six Beliefs)
cards.summary: Define up to six beliefs a prospect must hold to buy, so copy has a checklist of mindset shifts to achieve.
cards.use_when: Structuring advertorial narrative and objection handling around the belief shifts required before a visitor will purchase.
steps: Adopt the source's framing: marketing is a game of belief change — prospects arrive with existing beliefs and act in accordance with them, so copy must shift limiting beliefs into empowering ones.
Prompt the model to produce at most six beliefs that, if the prospect holds all of them, mean they will positively buy the product.
Write beliefs as first-person mindset statements, e.g. 'I believe my current method is inefficient and costly.'
Save the output as a PDF — foundational document number four — and treat it as the alignment checklist for every draft.
When reviewing any advertorial draft, verify it drives each necessary belief; the source's position is that if all six are covered, the copy job is essentially done.
Reuse the beliefs doc across advertorials, VSLs and ads for the same offer.
caveats: The maximum of six is the presenter's own constraint for keeping copy focused, not an industry standard.
A belief list is a diagnostic for copy, not proof that purchase will follow.
cards.source_name: how i write advertorial landing pages that make me $1.3m_mo only using AI (prompts included).docx

cards.title: Swipe Selection and Structuring an Advertorial Draft
cards.summary: Choose a currently successful competitor advertorial as a structural reference and prompt AI to write your draft in halves.
cards.use_when: Drafting a new advertorial landing page and needing a proven structure plus a workable drafting process.
steps: Find an advertorial that is currently running successfully in your market; convert that page to PDF and upload it as the structural swipe.
Upload your four foundational documents alongside the swipe so the model writes your copy, not the competitor's.
Prompt for the first half only — the source warns that asking for a full ~2,000-word advertorial in one response degrades quality because of token limits and truncation.
Review the first half; if the angle is wrong, iterate on angle before continuing, since drafting should be conversational at this stage.
Prompt for the second half, then assemble both halves into one advertorial document.

In the demo the model produced a headline using an old direct-response open-loop structure ('I couldn't sleep at night terrified... until I discovered this new device') without being told to; the source treats the headline as the highest-leverage element to split test.
Prefer the 'answer in chat' output setting rather than the side view; the presenter reports cleaner outputs that way (his personal, admittedly biased preference).
caveats: Token-limit chunking is the presenter's practical workaround; exact limits vary by model and plan.
The source's claim that the headline carries roughly 90% of advertorial performance is a direct-response opinion, not a measured figure.
cards.source_name: how i write advertorial landing pages that make me $1.3m_mo only using AI (prompts included).docx

cards.title: Chiefing: AI Review Against Foundational Docs, Then Human Pass
cards.summary: Edit process where AI checks the draft against research, beliefs and mechanism, then a human removes friction from the read.
cards.use_when: Final review of an advertorial before spending money on paid traffic to that landing page.
steps: Upload the completed advertorial draft back into the chat and prompt the model to evaluate it against the four foundational documents: research, avatar sheet, offer brief and necessary beliefs.

Have it confirm the draft hits each necessary belief, presents the unique mechanism clearly and handles objections; the source's ideal is that objections are handled before the prospect ever reaches the sales page, not relegated to an FAQ.
Check that the review covers emotional storytelling, problem identification, risk reversal and alignment with the level of consciousness and stage of sophistication.

Take the AI's suggested improvement areas as new angle options — in the demo, a 'whistleblower' angle (an insider exposing that heating companies keep bills high) was flagged as a strong unexploited angle.

Then personally read the full copy and where the flow is not completely natural, rewrite it; the source cites the 'slippery slide' rule — copy should read like a greased slide, and any bump costs conversions.
Only ship after the human pass; the source explicitly says AI chiefing alone is not the end of the process.
caveats: The slippery-slide principle is attributed to an unnamed famous copywriter; the presenter could not recall the name.
AI review can validate alignment without catching weak angles — treat its improvement suggestions as options, not instructions.
cards.source_name: how i write advertorial landing pages that make me $1.3m_mo only using AI (prompts included).docx

cards.title: Slippery Slide Editing: Finding and Removing Bumps
cards.summary: Practical editing pass for advertorial copy that locates friction points where the reader might stop sliding toward the CTA.
cards.use_when: Line-level editing of advertorial or landing page copy before launch to paid traffic.
steps: Read the full advertorial end to end as a prospect would, watching for moments where you personally get stuck or the sentence flow stalls.
Mark any illogical ordering of words or ideas as a 'bump' — the source's rule is that copy should flow so naturally the reader slides from headline to call to action without friction.
Rewrite flagged passages to restore natural sequence rather than adding more claims; the cause is usually structure, not missing information.
Cross-check the edited passage still carries its assigned necessary belief so the fix doesn't strip out persuasive function.
Repeat until no passage causes a stall, then hand off to traffic — the source frames imperfections here as directly costing conversions.
caveats: The rule is heuristic and drawn from direct-response tradition via the presenter's recollection, not an experiment.
Flow alone does not validate the offer or headline; those carry more weight in the source's own view.
cards.source_name: how i write advertorial landing pages that make me $1.3m_mo only using AI (prompts included).docx

cards.title: Driving Traffic to an Advertorial with Open-Loop Headlines
cards.summary: Use curiosity-driven, unresolved headlines in advertorials so paid traffic clicks through and reads rather than bouncing.
cards.use_when: Writing the headline block and above-the-fold copy for an advertorial that will receive cold paid traffic.
steps: Open with a large open loop — a headline that raises a question or tension the reader must resolve by continuing; the source describes this as exactly what you want in an advertorial.

Model the structure on the old direct-response pattern of personal fear or struggle followed by a discovery reveal, as seen in the demo headline about sleepless nights over heating bills culminating in finding a device.
Include emotional specificity tied to the researched pain, e.g. family stress over energy costs, rather than abstract benefit language.
Keep the first half of the advertorial carrying the story and open loop; do not resolve the loop before the reader reaches the mechanism and offer.
Consider testing multiple angles via the advertorial headline, since the source treats the headline as the element that pulls the most weight in a split test.
Adapt copy from the competitor swipe only at the structural level, filling it with your own research-sourced detail so the story is credible for your brand.
caveats: The commonly repeated 'headline = 90% of performance' figure is the presenter's assertion, not a documented benchmark.
Open-loop headlines can clash with brand-safety or claims policies on some ad platforms; check platform rules before running.
cards.source_name: how i write advertorial landing pages that make me $1.3m_mo only using AI (prompts included).docx

cards.title: Handling Objections Before the Sales Page
cards.summary: Shift the norm from FAQ-based objection handling to pre-handling objections inside the advertorial itself.
cards.use_when: Structuring advertorial narrative for a high-consideration or price-sensitive product where prospects arrive skeptical.
steps: Do not confine objection handling to a FAQ block at the bottom of the page; the source states the ideal is to handle objections before the prospect even reaches the sales page.
Identify the primary objections from your avatar research and necessary-beliefs work — the demo's core objection was affordability and fear of another huge bill.
Weave responses into the story and mechanism sections naturally so the reader encounters the reframe while following the narrative, not as a defensive paragraph.
Include risk reversal in the advertorial as part of that handling, which the source connects directly to affordability objections in the demo.
Confirm during your chiefing review that objections surfaced by AI review have actually been addressed in the draft, not just noted.
caveats: This is a direct-response convention the presenter advocates, not a rule with published test data.
Over-handling objections too early can weaken the message or create doubts the reader didn't have; judge against your own audience research.
cards.source_name: how i write advertorial landing pages that make me $1.3m_mo only using AI (prompts included).docx

cards.title: Choosing Markets and Angles You're Willing to Sell To
cards.summary: The presenter's rule on avoiding price-driven audiences and reframing around premium positioning, plus how to repurpose the resulting angle insight.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to build an advertorial offer for a market whose dominant desire is lowest price.
steps: Recognise the signal: if your research shows the primary motivation is affordability or the cheapest option, the source says this is a race to the bottom with low margins and he prefers not to compete on price.
Prefer selling premium products to premium audiences where premium marketing, messaging and copy align — he cites Walmart and Amazon as competitors you cannot out-price.

If you nonetheless build in a price-sensitive market, reframe the advertorial angle around a dominating desire other than cheapness (in the demo this could mean focusing on the mechanism or the whistleblower angle rather than savings).
Use the necessary-beliefs and offer-brief documents to test whether the angle you've chosen still matches the audience's actual dominant motivation.
Treat this as a positioning decision made before writing, since the angle drives the swipe selection and the headline.
caveats: This is the presenter's stated preference and opinion, not a general rule; some operators deliberately serve price-sensitive markets at volume.
The demo's affordability research is his example market, not evidence about any specific niche.
cards.source_name: how i write advertorial landing pages that make me $1.3m_mo only using AI (prompts included).docx

cards.title: Keeping Foundational Documents Reusable Across Copy Assets
cards.summary: Treat the research doc, avatar sheet, offer brief and necessary beliefs as a persistent brand asset set that powers all future AI copy.
cards.use_when: Scaling content production across advertorials, VSLs, ads and landing pages for an existing product or brand.
steps: Store all four foundational documents as PDFs so they can be re-uploaded into any new AI copy session quickly.
Accept the upfront cost: the source describes the research and foundational-docs phase as the hard part that only has to be done once per brand or offer.
When starting any new copy asset, upload the four documents together and prompt the model to analyse each one first — the source uses this step to refresh the model's memory before drafting.
Add to the documents whenever new research becomes available; quality of output tracks quality of input.
Expect speedup for downstream assets (ads, VSLs, landing page copy) once the set exists, since the model no longer needs to rediscover the audience and offer.
caveats: Documents are only as current as the research behind them; stale research propagates into every downstream asset.
The recommended model version and upload mechanics will change over time — re-verify the current interface.
